The **Kordofan giraffe** (_**Giraffa antiquorum**_[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kordofan_giraffe#cite_note-:1-2) or _**Giraffa camelopardalis antiquorum**_) is a [species](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Species "Species") or [subspecies](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Subspecies "Subspecies") of [giraffe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Giraffe "Giraffe") found in [northern Cameroon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Northern_Cameroon "Northern Cameroon"), southern [Chad](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chad "Chad"), the [Central African Republic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Central_African_Republic "Central African Republic"), and possibly [western Sudan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Western_Sudan "Western Sudan").[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kordofan_giraffe#cite_note-range-3) They usually live in [tree savannas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Savanna "Savanna"), [bush savannas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steppe "Steppe") and [thorn savannas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Savanna "Savanna").[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kordofan_giraffe#cite_note-:0-4) Compared to most other subspecies, the Kordofan giraffe is relatively small at 3.8 to 4.7 m (12 ft 6 in to 15 ft 5 in),[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kordofan_giraffe#cite_note-5) with more irregular spots on the inner legs. There are around 2,300 individuals living in the wild.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kordofan_giraffe#cite_note-6) In the wild, female Kordofan giraffes live in loose groups, whilst males live solitary.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kordofan_giraffe#cite_note-:0-4) They have an average lifespan of around 35 years.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kordofan_giraffe#cite_note-:0-4)

_[The Christian Science Monitor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Christian\_Science\_Monitor "The Christian Science Monitor")_ lists only 38 individuals being alive in the embattled [Garamba National Park](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Garamba_National_Park "Garamba National Park") in [The Democratic Republic of Congo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Democratic_Republic_of_Congo "The Democratic Republic of Congo") due to [poaching](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Poaching "Poaching"); their skin is used for [luxury goods](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luxury_goods "Luxury goods") and they are said to produce enough meat to feed poachers for weeks.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_] Recent genetic studies also shows distinct [genetic populations](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Genetic_populations "Genetic populations") of giraffes that makes conservation of these subspecies even more important.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kordofan_giraffe#cite_note-7)

The population in the Bénoué Complex, Cameroon (a landscape that consists of three national parks: [Bénoué National Park](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/B%C3%A9nou%C3%A9_National_Park "Bénoué National Park"), [Faro National Park](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Faro_National_Park "Faro National Park"), [Bouba Njida National Park](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bouba_Njida_National_Park "Bouba Njida National Park"); interconnected by 29 hunting zones), numbers fewer than 300 individuals as of 2023.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kordofan_giraffe#cite_note-onlinelibrary.wiley.com-8) Illegal hunting represents the greatest threat to the subspecies, particularly in [Bénoué National Park](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/B%C3%A9nou%C3%A9_National_Park "Bénoué National Park"), where it may become locally extinct without further conservation interventions.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kordofan_giraffe#cite_note-onlinelibrary.wiley.com-8)

The Kordofan giraffe eats a variety of sticks, leaves and bark, usually of [Acacia trees](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Acacia "Acacia"). Additionally they eat grasses, buds, as well as seeds.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kordofan_giraffe#cite_note-Baselzoo-9) Like other giraffes, they classify as herbivores.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kordofan_giraffe#cite_note-:0-4)

## Taxonomy

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Kordofan_giraffe&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Taxonomy")]

Its English name is a reference to [Kordofan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kordofan "Kordofan") in [Sudan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sudan "Sudan").[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kordofan_giraffe#cite_note-:1-2)[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kordofan_giraffe#cite_note-range-3)

## Habitat

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Kordofan_giraffe&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Habitat")]

They are naturally found in northern [Cameroon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cameroon "Cameroon"), [Chad](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chad "Chad"), [Central African Republic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Central_African_Republic "Central African Republic") and [western Sudan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sudan_(region) "Sudan (region)").[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kordofan_giraffe#cite_note-range-3)[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kordofan_giraffe#cite_note-:0-4)[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kordofan_giraffe#cite_note-Baselzoo-9) Kordofan giraffe live in [steppes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steppe "Steppe"), as well as [bush](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Savanna "Savanna"), [tree](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Savanna "Savanna") and [shrub savannas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Savanna "Savanna").[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kordofan_giraffe#cite_note-:0-4) Historically some confusion has existed over the exact range limit of this subspecies compared to the [West African giraffe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/West_African_giraffe "West African giraffe"), with populations in e.g. northern [Cameroon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cameroon "Cameroon") formerly assigned to the latter.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kordofan_giraffe#cite_note-Baselzoo-9) Genetic work has also revealed that all "[West African giraffe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/West_African_giraffe "West African giraffe")" in European [zoos](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zoo "Zoo") are in fact Kordofan giraffe.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kordofan_giraffe#cite_note-Baselzoo-9) It has been suggested that the [Nigerian giraffe's](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/West_African_giraffe "West African giraffe") ancestor dispersed from East to North Africa during the [Quaternary](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quaternary "Quaternary") period and thereafter migrated to its current [Sahel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sahel "Sahel") distribution in West Africa in response to the development of the [Sahara](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sahara "Sahara") desert.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kordofan_giraffe#cite_note-range-3)

## Appearance

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Kordofan_giraffe&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Appearance")]

The Kordofan giraffe has spots similarly to other giraffe subspecies. They are [even-toed ungulates](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Artiodactyl "Artiodactyl") and walk on long legs. Compared to other subspecies they are rather small; males are on average 6 m (19 ft 8 in) tall, females reach a height of 4.5 m (14 ft 9 in).[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kordofan_giraffe#cite_note-Baselzoo-9) Their shoulder height lies between 2 metres (6 ft 7 in) for females to 3.5 metres (11 ft 6 in) for males.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kordofan_giraffe#cite_note-Baselzoo-9) On top of that they have more irregular spots on the inner legs.

They have a blue tongue, which is around 50 centimetres (1 ft 8 in) long.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kordofan_giraffe#cite_note-:0-4)

## Diet

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Kordofan_giraffe&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Diet")]

Like other giraffe subspecies, the Kordofan giraffe is a [herbivore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Herbivore "Herbivore"). Its diet consist of a variety of grasses, shrubs, buds, branches, leaves and bark, as well as seeds.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kordofan_giraffe#cite_note-:0-4)[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kordofan_giraffe#cite_note-Baselzoo-9) Their main food source comes from the [Acacia trees](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Acacia "Acacia").

## Conservation

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Kordofan_giraffe&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Conservation")]

Kordofan giraffe is one of most endangered giraffe subspecies. The population of kordofan giraffe declined more than 80% for last 35 years, IUCN Red List has classified the Kordofan giraffe as Critically Endangered species in 2018.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kordofan_giraffe#cite_note-GCFchad-10)[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kordofan_giraffe#cite_note-iucn-1)

[![Image 8](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/7/7e/Kordofan_giraffe_in_Garamba_National_Park.jpg/250px-Kordofan_giraffe_in_Garamba_National_Park.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Kordofan_giraffe_in_Garamba_National_Park.jpg)

Kordofan giraffe in the [Garamba National Park](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Garamba_National_Park "Garamba National Park"), DRC

In the [Garamba National Park](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Garamba_National_Park "Garamba National Park") in DRC, their population was declined from 300 in 1976 to 100 in 2008.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kordofan_giraffe#cite_note-11) Another estimate is from 356 in 1993 to only 86 in 2007.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kordofan_giraffe#cite_note-thetimes-12) There also estimate that 86 in 2003 and only 38 in 2016.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kordofan_giraffe#cite_note-13) Most recent estimate is from 71 in 2022 to over 80 in 2024.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kordofan_giraffe#cite_note-14) Poaching is the greatest threat to Garamba's giraffe population.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kordofan_giraffe#cite_note-thetimes-12)[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kordofan_giraffe#cite_note-GCF_DRC-15) It has brought Giraffe Conservation Foundation (GCF) collaboration with ICCN and African Parks and DRC's wildlife authority to save last giraffes in DRC since 2016.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kordofan_giraffe#cite_note-GCF_DRC-15) Fortunately, DRC government have successfully increased in Kordofan giraffe population in park to more than 90 individuals.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kordofan_giraffe#cite_note-GCF_DRC-15)

[![Image 9](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/7/7d/Waza-NP-Giraffes.jpg/250px-Waza-NP-Giraffes.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Waza-NP-Giraffes.jpg)

A group of Kordofan giraffes in the [Waza National Park](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Waza_National_Park "Waza National Park"), Cameroon

In Bénoué Complex on Cameroon(a landscape that consists of three national parks: [Bénoué National Park](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/B%C3%A9nou%C3%A9_National_Park "Bénoué National Park"), [Faro National Park](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Faro_National_Park "Faro National Park"), [Bouba Njida National Park](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bouba_Njida_National_Park "Bouba Njida National Park")); interconnected by 29 hunting zones), it is estimated fewer than 300 population remained in 2023. Illegal hunting is a major threat to giraffe in the Bénoué National Park, where it may become locally extinct without further conservation efforts.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kordofan_giraffe#cite_note-16) In an aerial survey by Wildlife Conservation Society of [Waza National Park](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Waza_National_Park "Waza National Park") it was revealed that at least 350 individuals remained.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kordofan_giraffe#cite_note-GCFcameroon-17) GCF drafting the first-ever National Giraffe Conservation Strategy and Action Plan with together Cameroon government, to help conservation efforts for Kordofan giraffe in the country.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kordofan_giraffe#cite_note-GCFcameroon-17)

[![Image 10](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/e/ee/Girafe_du_parc_national_de_Zakouma.jpg/250px-Girafe_du_parc_national_de_Zakouma.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Girafe_du_parc_national_de_Zakouma.jpg)

Kordofan giraffe in the [Zakouma National Park](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zakouma_National_Park "Zakouma National Park"), Chad

[Zakouma National Park](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zakouma_National_Park "Zakouma National Park") of [Chad](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chad "Chad") is home to 60% of Kordofan giraffe remaining on earth.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kordofan_giraffe#cite_note-GCFchad-10) According to a series of aerial surveys in park between 2005 and 2016, population of giraffe in park increased from 292 to 947.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kordofan_giraffe#cite_note-iucn-1) GCF drafting the first-ever conservation efforts for Kordofan giraffe in the country in collaboration with the African Parks.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kordofan_giraffe#cite_note-GCFchad-10) According to the tracking of giraffes' movements using GPS satellite tagging, some giraffe in the park spend significant time at boundaries of the park.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kordofan_giraffe#cite_note-GCFchad-10)

The **Kordofan giraffe** (_**Giraffa antiquorum**_[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kordofan_giraffe#cite_note-:1-2) or _**Giraffa camelopardalis antiquorum**_) is a [species](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Species "Species") or [subspecies](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Subspecies "Subspecies") of [giraffe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Giraffe "Giraffe") found in [northern Cameroon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Northern_Cameroon "Northern Cameroon"), southern [Chad](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chad "Chad"), the [Central African Republic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Central_African_Republic "Central African Republic"), and possibly [western Sudan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Western_Sudan "Western Sudan").[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kordofan_giraffe#cite_note-range-3) They usually live in [tree savannas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Savanna "Savanna"), [bush savannas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steppe "Steppe") and [thorn savannas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Savanna "Savanna").[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kordofan_giraffe#cite_note-:0-4) Compared to most other subspecies, the Kordofan giraffe is relatively small at 3.8 to 4.7 m (12 ft 6 in to 15 ft 5 in),[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kordofan_giraffe#cite_note-5) with more irregular spots on the inner legs. There are around 2,300 individuals living in the wild.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kordofan_giraffe#cite_note-6) In the wild, female Kordofan giraffes live in loose groups, whilst males live solitary.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kordofan_giraffe#cite_note-:0-4) They have an average lifespan of around 35 years.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kordofan_giraffe#cite_note-:0-4)

_[The Christian Science Monitor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Christian\_Science\_Monitor "The Christian Science Monitor")_ lists only 38 individuals being alive in the embattled [Garamba National Park](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Garamba_National_Park "Garamba National Park") in [The Democratic Republic of Congo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Democratic_Republic_of_Congo "The Democratic Republic of Congo") due to [poaching](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Poaching "Poaching"); their skin is used for [luxury goods](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luxury_goods "Luxury goods") and they are said to produce enough meat to feed poachers for weeks.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_] Recent genetic studies also shows distinct [genetic populations](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Genetic_populations "Genetic populations") of giraffes that makes conservation of these subspecies even more important.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kordofan_giraffe#cite_note-7)

The population in the Bénoué Complex, Cameroon (a landscape that consists of three national parks: [Bénoué National Park](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/B%C3%A9nou%C3%A9_National_Park "Bénoué National Park"), [Faro National Park](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Faro_National_Park "Faro National Park"), [Bouba Njida National Park](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bouba_Njida_National_Park "Bouba Njida National Park"); interconnected by 29 hunting zones), numbers fewer than 300 individuals as of 2023.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kordofan_giraffe#cite_note-onlinelibrary.wiley.com-8) Illegal hunting represents the greatest threat to the subspecies, particularly in [Bénoué National Park](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/B%C3%A9nou%C3%A9_National_Park "Bénoué National Park"), where it may become locally extinct without further conservation interventions.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kordofan_giraffe#cite_note-onlinelibrary.wiley.com-8)

The Kordofan giraffe eats a variety of sticks, leaves and bark, usually of [Acacia trees](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Acacia "Acacia"). Additionally they eat grasses, buds, as well as seeds.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kordofan_giraffe#cite_note-Baselzoo-9) Like other giraffes, they classify as herbivores.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kordofan_giraffe#cite_note-:0-4)

## Taxonomy

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Kordofan_giraffe&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Taxonomy")]

Its English name is a reference to [Kordofan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kordofan "Kordofan") in [Sudan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sudan "Sudan").[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kordofan_giraffe#cite_note-:1-2)[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kordofan_giraffe#cite_note-range-3)

## Habitat

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Kordofan_giraffe&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Habitat")]

They are naturally found in northern [Cameroon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cameroon "Cameroon"), [Chad](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chad "Chad"), [Central African Republic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Central_African_Republic "Central African Republic") and [western Sudan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sudan_(region) "Sudan (region)").[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kordofan_giraffe#cite_note-range-3)[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kordofan_giraffe#cite_note-:0-4)[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kordofan_giraffe#cite_note-Baselzoo-9) Kordofan giraffe live in [steppes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steppe "Steppe"), as well as [bush](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Savanna "Savanna"), [tree](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Savanna "Savanna") and [shrub savannas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Savanna "Savanna").[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kordofan_giraffe#cite_note-:0-4) Historically some confusion has existed over the exact range limit of this subspecies compared to the [West African giraffe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/West_African_giraffe "West African giraffe"), with populations in e.g. northern [Cameroon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cameroon "Cameroon") formerly assigned to the latter.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kordofan_giraffe#cite_note-Baselzoo-9) Genetic work has also revealed that all "[West African giraffe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/West_African_giraffe "West African giraffe")" in European [zoos](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zoo "Zoo") are in fact Kordofan giraffe.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kordofan_giraffe#cite_note-Baselzoo-9) It has been suggested that the [Nigerian giraffe's](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/West_African_giraffe "West African giraffe") ancestor dispersed from East to North Africa during the [Quaternary](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quaternary "Quaternary") period and thereafter migrated to its current [Sahel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sahel "Sahel") distribution in West Africa in response to the development of the [Sahara](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sahara "Sahara") desert.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kordofan_giraffe#cite_note-range-3)

## Appearance

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Kordofan_giraffe&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Appearance")]

The Kordofan giraffe has spots similarly to other giraffe subspecies. They are [even-toed ungulates](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Artiodactyl "Artiodactyl") and walk on long legs. Compared to other subspecies they are rather small; males are on average 6 m (19 ft 8 in) tall, females reach a height of 4.5 m (14 ft 9 in).[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kordofan_giraffe#cite_note-Baselzoo-9) Their shoulder height lies between 2 metres (6 ft 7 in) for females to 3.5 metres (11 ft 6 in) for males.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kordofan_giraffe#cite_note-Baselzoo-9) On top of that they have more irregular spots on the inner legs.

They have a blue tongue, which is around 50 centimetres (1 ft 8 in) long.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kordofan_giraffe#cite_note-:0-4)

## Diet

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Kordofan_giraffe&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Diet")]

Like other giraffe subspecies, the Kordofan giraffe is a [herbivore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Herbivore "Herbivore"). Its diet consist of a variety of grasses, shrubs, buds, branches, leaves and bark, as well as seeds.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kordofan_giraffe#cite_note-:0-4)[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kordofan_giraffe#cite_note-Baselzoo-9) Their main food source comes from the [Acacia trees](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Acacia "Acacia").

## Conservation

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Kordofan_giraffe&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Conservation")]

Kordofan giraffe is one of most endangered giraffe subspecies. The population of kordofan giraffe declined more than 80% for last 35 years, IUCN Red List has classified the Kordofan giraffe as Critically Endangered species in 2018.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kordofan_giraffe#cite_note-GCFchad-10)[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kordofan_giraffe#cite_note-iucn-1)

[![Image 8](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/7/7e/Kordofan_giraffe_in_Garamba_National_Park.jpg/250px-Kordofan_giraffe_in_Garamba_National_Park.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Kordofan_giraffe_in_Garamba_National_Park.jpg)

Kordofan giraffe in the [Garamba National Park](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Garamba_National_Park "Garamba National Park"), DRC

In the [Garamba National Park](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Garamba_National_Park "Garamba National Park") in DRC, their population was declined from 300 in 1976 to 100 in 2008.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kordofan_giraffe#cite_note-11) Another estimate is from 356 in 1993 to only 86 in 2007.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kordofan_giraffe#cite_note-thetimes-12) There also estimate that 86 in 2003 and only 38 in 2016.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kordofan_giraffe#cite_note-13) Most recent estimate is from 71 in 2022 to over 80 in 2024.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kordofan_giraffe#cite_note-14) Poaching is the greatest threat to Garamba's giraffe population.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kordofan_giraffe#cite_note-thetimes-12)[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kordofan_giraffe#cite_note-GCF_DRC-15) It has brought Giraffe Conservation Foundation (GCF) collaboration with ICCN and African Parks and DRC's wildlife authority to save last giraffes in DRC since 2016.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kordofan_giraffe#cite_note-GCF_DRC-15) Fortunately, DRC government have successfully increased in Kordofan giraffe population in park to more than 90 individuals.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kordofan_giraffe#cite_note-GCF_DRC-15)

[![Image 9](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/7/7d/Waza-NP-Giraffes.jpg/250px-Waza-NP-Giraffes.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Waza-NP-Giraffes.jpg)

A group of Kordofan giraffes in the [Waza National Park](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Waza_National_Park "Waza National Park"), Cameroon

In Bénoué Complex on Cameroon(a landscape that consists of three national parks: [Bénoué National Park](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/B%C3%A9nou%C3%A9_National_Park "Bénoué National Park"), [Faro National Park](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Faro_National_Park "Faro National Park"), [Bouba Njida National Park](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bouba_Njida_National_Park "Bouba Njida National Park")); interconnected by 29 hunting zones), it is estimated fewer than 300 population remained in 2023. Illegal hunting is a major threat to giraffe in the Bénoué National Park, where it may become locally extinct without further conservation efforts.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kordofan_giraffe#cite_note-16) In an aerial survey by Wildlife Conservation Society of [Waza National Park](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Waza_National_Park "Waza National Park") it was revealed that at least 350 individuals remained.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kordofan_giraffe#cite_note-GCFcameroon-17) GCF drafting the first-ever National Giraffe Conservation Strategy and Action Plan with together Cameroon government, to help conservation efforts for Kordofan giraffe in the country.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kordofan_giraffe#cite_note-GCFcameroon-17)

[![Image 10](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/e/ee/Girafe_du_parc_national_de_Zakouma.jpg/250px-Girafe_du_parc_national_de_Zakouma.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Girafe_du_parc_national_de_Zakouma.jpg)

Kordofan giraffe in the [Zakouma National Park](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zakouma_National_Park "Zakouma National Park"), Chad

[Zakouma National Park](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zakouma_National_Park "Zakouma National Park") of [Chad](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chad "Chad") is home to 60% of Kordofan giraffe remaining on earth.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kordofan_giraffe#cite_note-GCFchad-10) According to a series of aerial surveys in park between 2005 and 2016, population of giraffe in park increased from 292 to 947.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kordofan_giraffe#cite_note-iucn-1) GCF drafting the first-ever conservation efforts for Kordofan giraffe in the country in collaboration with the African Parks.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kordofan_giraffe#cite_note-GCFchad-10) According to the tracking of giraffes' movements using GPS satellite tagging, some giraffe in the park spend significant time at boundaries of the park.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kordofan_giraffe#cite_note-GCFchad-10)

**Garamba National Park** ([French](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/French_language "French language"): _Parc national de la Garamba_) is a [national park](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_park "National park") in the north-eastern [Democratic Republic of the Congo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Democratic_Republic_of_the_Congo "Democratic Republic of the Congo") covering nearly 5,200 km 2 (2,000 sq mi). It is among Africa's oldest parks and was designated a [World Heritage Site](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_Heritage_Site "World Heritage Site") by [UNESCO](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UNESCO "UNESCO") in 1980 for its protection of critical habitat for [northern white rhinoceroses](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Northern_white_rhinoceros "Northern white rhinoceros"), [African elephants](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/African_elephant "African elephant"), [hippopotamuses](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hippopotamus "Hippopotamus"), and [giraffes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Giraffe "Giraffe").[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Garamba_National_Park#cite_note-unesco-1) Garamba National Park has been managed by [African Parks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/African_Parks "African Parks") in partnership with the [Institut Congolais pour la Conservation de la Nature](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Institut_Congolais_pour_la_Conservation_de_la_Nature "Institut Congolais pour la Conservation de la Nature") since 2005.

## Overview

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Garamba_National_Park&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Overview")]

Garamba National Park was established in 1938 and covers an area of 4,900 km 2 (1,900 sq mi) in northeastern Democratic Republic of the Congo. It is bounded by [Gangala-na-Bodio Hunting Reserve](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gangala-na-Bodio_Hunting_Reserve "Gangala-na-Bodio Hunting Reserve") on the west, south, and east, and borders [South Sudan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Sudan "South Sudan") on the north and northeast. It is part of the Sudano–[Guinean savanna](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guinea_savanna_woodland "Guinea savanna woodland") zone.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Garamba_National_Park#cite_note-2)[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Garamba_National_Park#cite_note-NG-3) The park is one of Africa's oldest protected areas.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Garamba_National_Park#cite_note-Gettleman-4) It lies in the transition zone between two centres of [endemism](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Endemism "Endemism"): Guinea-Congolian and Guinean-Sudanese savanna. These two biogeographic zones support a variety of wildlife, which have experienced population declines in recent decades because of [poaching](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Poaching "Poaching").[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Garamba_National_Park#cite_note-Canby-5) ICCN rangers, augmented with soldiers of the [Armed Forces of the Democratic Republic of the Congo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Armed_Forces_of_the_Democratic_Republic_of_the_Congo "Armed Forces of the Democratic Republic of the Congo"), work to protect Garamba from poachers and rebel groups.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Garamba_National_Park#cite_note-Canby-5)

## History

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Garamba_National_Park&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: History")]

The national park was established in 1938.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Garamba_National_Park#cite_note-Gettleman-4)[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Garamba_National_Park#cite_note-Avant-6)

The park was designated a World Heritage Site by UNESCO in 1980, and was included on the [specialized agency](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_specialized_agencies_of_the_United_Nations "List of specialized agencies of the United Nations")'s List of World Heritage in Danger from 1984–1992.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Garamba_National_Park#cite_note-7)[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Garamba_National_Park#cite_note-8) Between 1991 and 1993, 50,000 Sudanese refugees settled outside Garamba after being displaced by the [Sudan People's Liberation Army](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sudan_People's_Liberation_Army "Sudan People's Liberation Army"), resulting in increased poaching. There were reportedly 121 conflicts between poachers and park rangers between 1993 and 1995, and more than 900 weapons recovered by rangers during 1991–1996.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Garamba_National_Park#cite_note-Avant-6) The [International Rhino Foundation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Rhino_Foundation "International Rhino Foundation") provided funding for patrol vehicles in 1994, and ranger salaries in 1995. In February 1996, two rhinos—one male, Bawesi, and Juliet, a pregnant female—were killed.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Garamba_National_Park#cite_note-Avant-6) Garamba was added back to the danger list in 1996 because of northern white rhinoceros poaching.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Garamba_National_Park#cite_note-BBC-9)[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Garamba_National_Park#cite_note-Heale-10) Following a number of defeats during the [First Congo War](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/First_Congo_War "First Congo War") and [Second Sudanese Civil War](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Second_Sudanese_Civil_War "Second Sudanese Civil War"), most importantly [Operation Thunderbolt](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Operation_Thunderbolt_(1997) "Operation Thunderbolt (1997)"), the [Ugandan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Uganda "Uganda") insurgents of [WNBF](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/West_Nile_Bank_Front "West Nile Bank Front") and [UNRF (II)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Uganda_National_Rescue_Front "Uganda National Rescue Front") took refuge in Garamba National Park in 1997.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Garamba_National_Park#cite_note-FOOTNOTEPrunier2004377-11) Organizations like the [Frankfurt Zoological Society](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Frankfurt_Zoological_Society "Frankfurt Zoological Society"), [International Union for Conservation of Nature](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Union_for_Conservation_of_Nature "International Union for Conservation of Nature"), and [World Wildlife Fund](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_Wildlife_Fund "World Wildlife Fund") have also worked with local authorities to rehabilitate Garamba.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Garamba_National_Park#cite_note-Avant-6)

African Parks' anti-poaching efforts have reportedly been successful at reducing animal deaths.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Garamba_National_Park#cite_note-Nicolon-12) According to [BBC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BBC "BBC"), Garamba's management has been financed by the [European Union](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/European_Union "European Union") and private donors.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Garamba_National_Park#cite_note-BBC-9) Other contributors have included the [United States Agency for International Development](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Agency_for_International_Development "United States Agency for International Development"), [United States Fish and Wildlife Service](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Fish_and_Wildlife_Service "United States Fish and Wildlife Service"), Wildcat Foundation, and [World Bank](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_Bank "World Bank"),[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Garamba_National_Park#cite_note-13) according to African Parks.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Garamba_National_Park#cite_note-14)

Since 2005, the protected area is considered a [Lion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Central_African_lion "Central African lion") Conservation Unit together with [Domaine Chasse Bili Uere](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Domaine_Chasse_Bili_Uere "Domaine Chasse Bili Uere").[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Garamba_National_Park#cite_note-15)

Poachers have killed at least 21 park rangers in the last decade, as of 2017, and security concerns have contributed to Garamba's struggle to establish itself as a tourist destination.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Garamba_National_Park#cite_note-NG-3)[Joseph Kony](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joseph_Kony "Joseph Kony")'s [Lord's Resistance Army](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lord's_Resistance_Army "Lord's Resistance Army") have used the park for sanctuary.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Garamba_National_Park#cite_note-Canby-5)[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Garamba_National_Park#cite_note-Nicolon-12)[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Garamba_National_Park#cite_note-Chandrasekaran-16) In 2009, the guerrilla group attacked Garamba's Nagero station, killing at least eight people, including two park rangers, and wounding an additional thirteen. Rebels also stole food and fuel, and destroyed several of the park's buildings.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Garamba_National_Park#cite_note-Nicolon-12) Poachers killed five rangers and three members of the Congolese armed forces in three conflicts in 2015,[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Garamba_National_Park#cite_note-Canby-5)[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Garamba_National_Park#cite_note-Dasgupta-17) and more were killed in October.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Garamba_National_Park#cite_note-ABC-18) In April 2016, poachers shot and killed three rangers, and wounded others (including Garamba's manager at the time),[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Garamba_National_Park#cite_note-Staufenberg-19)[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Garamba_National_Park#cite_note-CBS-20)[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Garamba_National_Park#cite_note-21) and two park rangers were killed by elephant poachers in April 2017.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Garamba_National_Park#cite_note-Nicolon-12)[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Garamba_National_Park#cite_note-Dasgupta-17)[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Garamba_National_Park#cite_note-CBS-20) According to photojournalist [Kate Brooks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kate_Brooks "Kate Brooks"), who filmed in Garamba for her documentary _The Last Animals_, thirteen park rangers and military personnel were killed defending Garamba between January 2015 and April 2017.[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Garamba_National_Park#cite_note-Brooks-22)

In 2017, National Geographic Documentary Films released _The Protectors: Walk in the Rangers' Shoes_, a short [virtual reality](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Virtual_reality "Virtual reality") documentary directed by [Kathryn Bigelow](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kathryn_Bigelow "Kathryn Bigelow") about the park's rangers and their efforts to protect Garamba's wildlife.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Garamba_National_Park#cite_note-NG-3)[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Garamba_National_Park#cite_note-Coyle-23) The [Tribeca Film Festival](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tribeca_Film_Festival "Tribeca Film Festival") posthumously awarded the Disruptor Award to rangers killed protecting Garamba "for their work and bravery in defending elephants", in April 2017.[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Garamba_National_Park#cite_note-Brooks-22)

### Mammals

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Garamba_National_Park&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Mammals")]

Garamba is home to 138 recorded mammal species,[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Garamba_National_Park#cite_note-Avant-6) including various [antelope](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antelope "Antelope"),[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Garamba_National_Park#cite_note-East-24)[African buffalo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/African_buffalo "African buffalo"), [African bush elephant](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/African_bush_elephant "African bush elephant"), [hyenas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hyena "Hyena"), [giant forest hog](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Giant_forest_hog "Giant forest hog"), [giraffes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Giraffe "Giraffe"), [hippopotamus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hippopotamus "Hippopotamus"), and lion.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Garamba_National_Park#cite_note-Canby-5)[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Garamba_National_Park#cite_note-Nicolon-12)[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Garamba_National_Park#cite_note-Dasgupta-17) The park hosts the country's only remaining population of giraffes, the Kordofan subspecies, and one of the country's largest remaining elephant populations.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Garamba_National_Park#cite_note-Canby-5)[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Garamba_National_Park#cite_note-Nicolon-12)

Garamba's elephants are considered a hybrid of the [African bush](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/African_bush_elephant "African bush elephant") and [African forest](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/African_forest_elephant "African forest elephant") subspecies.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Garamba_National_Park#cite_note-Canby-5) Poaching has reduced the park's elephant population in recent decades.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Garamba_National_Park#cite_note-Gettleman-4) There were around 2,800 elephants in 2011.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Garamba_National_Park#cite_note-Gettleman-4) In 2017, there were estimated to be fewer than 2,000 elephants in Garamba, a significant decline from the approximately 20,000 reported in the 1960s and 1970s.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Garamba_National_Park#cite_note-Canby-5)[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Garamba_National_Park#cite_note-NG-3)[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Garamba_National_Park#cite_note-Dasgupta-17) 22 elephants were killed in 2012,[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Garamba_National_Park#cite_note-Gettleman-4) and in 2014 poachers killed 68 of Garamba's elephants within two months.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Garamba_National_Park#cite_note-Dasgupta-17)[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Garamba_National_Park#cite_note-NYDN-25)[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Garamba_National_Park#cite_note-Min-26) Elephant poaching numbers declined from 98 in 2015 to three in 2022 in result to an effective law enforcement strategy.[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Garamba_National_Park#cite_note-27)

Reported giraffe population sizes have varied, but show a general decline in the 1990s and 2000s. The population's recorded peak was 300 in 1976, and more than 100 were reported in 2008.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Garamba_National_Park#cite_note-Nicolon-12) There were 356 giraffes in 1993, and only 86 by 2007.[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Garamba_National_Park#cite_note-TheTimes-28) There were 86 in 2003 and only 38 in 2016.[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Garamba_National_Park#cite_note-Hinckley-29) As of 2022, there were 71 giraffes in the park, and in 2024, over 80 Kordofan giraffes were allegedly present.[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Garamba_National_Park#cite_note-Parks-30) Poaching is the greatest threat to Garamba's giraffe population.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Garamba_National_Park#cite_note-Nicolon-12)[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Garamba_National_Park#cite_note-31)

The park once had the last wild population of the [northern white rhinoceros](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Northern_white_rhinoceros "Northern white rhinoceros").[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Garamba_National_Park#cite_note-Canby-5)[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Garamba_National_Park#cite_note-Gettleman-4)[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Garamba_National_Park#cite_note-Heale-10) Only fifteen northern white rhinos were reported in Garamba in the mid 1980s, prompting the park's inclusion on [UNESCO](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UNESCO "UNESCO")'s [List of World Heritage in Danger](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_World_Heritage_in_Danger "List of World Heritage in Danger").[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Garamba_National_Park#cite_note-Avant-6) In 2003–2004, there were reportedly between 20 and 25 white rhinos in the park.[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Garamba_National_Park#cite_note-Sieff-32)[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Garamba_National_Park#cite_note-Bisset-33)[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Garamba_National_Park#cite_note-Irish-34) In 2023, restoration efforts led to 16 white rhinos being moved from a private game reserve in South Africa to the park.[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Garamba_National_Park#cite_note-rhino-35)

### Birds

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Garamba_National_Park&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Birds")]

Some 286 bird species, including the [secretarybird](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Secretarybird "Secretarybird"),[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Garamba_National_Park#cite_note-Gettleman-4) have been recorded in the park.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Garamba_National_Park#cite_note-Avant-6) It has been designated an [Important Bird Area](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Important_Bird_Area "Important Bird Area") (IBA) by [BirdLife International](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BirdLife_International "BirdLife International") because it supports significant populations of many bird species.[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Garamba_National_Park#cite_note-bli-36)

### Threats

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Garamba_National_Park&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: Threats")]

Interactions between people and wild animals in and around the park has resulted in [human–wildlife conflict](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Human%E2%80%93wildlife_conflict "Human–wildlife conflict"). Local and South Sudanese poachers hunt for elephants, often in search of [ivory](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ivory_trade "Ivory trade").[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Garamba_National_Park#cite_note-Nicolon-12)[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Garamba_National_Park#cite_note-Dasgupta-17) Garamba's wildlife are also impacted by groups such as the Huda and [Wodaabe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wodaabe "Wodaabe") (or "Mbororo") seeking [pasture](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pasture "Pasture").[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Garamba_National_Park#cite_note-Nicolon-12)

**Garamba National Park** ([French](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/French_language "French language"): _Parc national de la Garamba_) is a [national park](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_park "National park") in the north-eastern [Democratic Republic of the Congo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Democratic_Republic_of_the_Congo "Democratic Republic of the Congo") covering nearly 5,200 km 2 (2,000 sq mi). It is among Africa's oldest parks and was designated a [World Heritage Site](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_Heritage_Site "World Heritage Site") by [UNESCO](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UNESCO "UNESCO") in 1980 for its protection of critical habitat for [northern white rhinoceroses](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Northern_white_rhinoceros "Northern white rhinoceros"), [African elephants](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/African_elephant "African elephant"), [hippopotamuses](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hippopotamus "Hippopotamus"), and [giraffes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Giraffe "Giraffe").[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Garamba_National_Park#cite_note-unesco-1) Garamba National Park has been managed by [African Parks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/African_Parks "African Parks") in partnership with the [Institut Congolais pour la Conservation de la Nature](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Institut_Congolais_pour_la_Conservation_de_la_Nature "Institut Congolais pour la Conservation de la Nature") since 2005.

## Overview

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Garamba_National_Park&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Overview")]

Garamba National Park was established in 1938 and covers an area of 4,900 km 2 (1,900 sq mi) in northeastern Democratic Republic of the Congo. It is bounded by [Gangala-na-Bodio Hunting Reserve](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gangala-na-Bodio_Hunting_Reserve "Gangala-na-Bodio Hunting Reserve") on the west, south, and east, and borders [South Sudan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Sudan "South Sudan") on the north and northeast. It is part of the Sudano–[Guinean savanna](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guinea_savanna_woodland "Guinea savanna woodland") zone.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Garamba_National_Park#cite_note-2)[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Garamba_National_Park#cite_note-NG-3) The park is one of Africa's oldest protected areas.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Garamba_National_Park#cite_note-Gettleman-4) It lies in the transition zone between two centres of [endemism](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Endemism "Endemism"): Guinea-Congolian and Guinean-Sudanese savanna. These two biogeographic zones support a variety of wildlife, which have experienced population declines in recent decades because of [poaching](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Poaching "Poaching").[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Garamba_National_Park#cite_note-Canby-5) ICCN rangers, augmented with soldiers of the [Armed Forces of the Democratic Republic of the Congo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Armed_Forces_of_the_Democratic_Republic_of_the_Congo "Armed Forces of the Democratic Republic of the Congo"), work to protect Garamba from poachers and rebel groups.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Garamba_National_Park#cite_note-Canby-5)

## History

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Garamba_National_Park&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: History")]

The national park was established in 1938.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Garamba_National_Park#cite_note-Gettleman-4)[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Garamba_National_Park#cite_note-Avant-6)

The park was designated a World Heritage Site by UNESCO in 1980, and was included on the [specialized agency](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_specialized_agencies_of_the_United_Nations "List of specialized agencies of the United Nations")'s List of World Heritage in Danger from 1984–1992.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Garamba_National_Park#cite_note-7)[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Garamba_National_Park#cite_note-8) Between 1991 and 1993, 50,000 Sudanese refugees settled outside Garamba after being displaced by the [Sudan People's Liberation Army](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sudan_People's_Liberation_Army "Sudan People's Liberation Army"), resulting in increased poaching. There were reportedly 121 conflicts between poachers and park rangers between 1993 and 1995, and more than 900 weapons recovered by rangers during 1991–1996.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Garamba_National_Park#cite_note-Avant-6) The [International Rhino Foundation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Rhino_Foundation "International Rhino Foundation") provided funding for patrol vehicles in 1994, and ranger salaries in 1995. In February 1996, two rhinos—one male, Bawesi, and Juliet, a pregnant female—were killed.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Garamba_National_Park#cite_note-Avant-6) Garamba was added back to the danger list in 1996 because of northern white rhinoceros poaching.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Garamba_National_Park#cite_note-BBC-9)[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Garamba_National_Park#cite_note-Heale-10) Following a number of defeats during the [First Congo War](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/First_Congo_War "First Congo War") and [Second Sudanese Civil War](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Second_Sudanese_Civil_War "Second Sudanese Civil War"), most importantly [Operation Thunderbolt](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Operation_Thunderbolt_(1997) "Operation Thunderbolt (1997)"), the [Ugandan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Uganda "Uganda") insurgents of [WNBF](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/West_Nile_Bank_Front "West Nile Bank Front") and [UNRF (II)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Uganda_National_Rescue_Front "Uganda National Rescue Front") took refuge in Garamba National Park in 1997.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Garamba_National_Park#cite_note-FOOTNOTEPrunier2004377-11) Organizations like the [Frankfurt Zoological Society](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Frankfurt_Zoological_Society "Frankfurt Zoological Society"), [International Union for Conservation of Nature](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Union_for_Conservation_of_Nature "International Union for Conservation of Nature"), and [World Wildlife Fund](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_Wildlife_Fund "World Wildlife Fund") have also worked with local authorities to rehabilitate Garamba.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Garamba_National_Park#cite_note-Avant-6)

African Parks' anti-poaching efforts have reportedly been successful at reducing animal deaths.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Garamba_National_Park#cite_note-Nicolon-12) According to [BBC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BBC "BBC"), Garamba's management has been financed by the [European Union](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/European_Union "European Union") and private donors.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Garamba_National_Park#cite_note-BBC-9) Other contributors have included the [United States Agency for International Development](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Agency_for_International_Development "United States Agency for International Development"), [United States Fish and Wildlife Service](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Fish_and_Wildlife_Service "United States Fish and Wildlife Service"), Wildcat Foundation, and [World Bank](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_Bank "World Bank"),[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Garamba_National_Park#cite_note-13) according to African Parks.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Garamba_National_Park#cite_note-14)

Since 2005, the protected area is considered a [Lion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Central_African_lion "Central African lion") Conservation Unit together with [Domaine Chasse Bili Uere](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Domaine_Chasse_Bili_Uere "Domaine Chasse Bili Uere").[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Garamba_National_Park#cite_note-15)

Poachers have killed at least 21 park rangers in the last decade, as of 2017, and security concerns have contributed to Garamba's struggle to establish itself as a tourist destination.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Garamba_National_Park#cite_note-NG-3)[Joseph Kony](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joseph_Kony "Joseph Kony")'s [Lord's Resistance Army](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lord's_Resistance_Army "Lord's Resistance Army") have used the park for sanctuary.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Garamba_National_Park#cite_note-Canby-5)[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Garamba_National_Park#cite_note-Nicolon-12)[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Garamba_National_Park#cite_note-Chandrasekaran-16) In 2009, the guerrilla group attacked Garamba's Nagero station, killing at least eight people, including two park rangers, and wounding an additional thirteen. Rebels also stole food and fuel, and destroyed several of the park's buildings.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Garamba_National_Park#cite_note-Nicolon-12) Poachers killed five rangers and three members of the Congolese armed forces in three conflicts in 2015,[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Garamba_National_Park#cite_note-Canby-5)[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Garamba_National_Park#cite_note-Dasgupta-17) and more were killed in October.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Garamba_National_Park#cite_note-ABC-18) In April 2016, poachers shot and killed three rangers, and wounded others (including Garamba's manager at the time),[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Garamba_National_Park#cite_note-Staufenberg-19)[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Garamba_National_Park#cite_note-CBS-20)[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Garamba_National_Park#cite_note-21) and two park rangers were killed by elephant poachers in April 2017.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Garamba_National_Park#cite_note-Nicolon-12)[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Garamba_National_Park#cite_note-Dasgupta-17)[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Garamba_National_Park#cite_note-CBS-20) According to photojournalist [Kate Brooks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kate_Brooks "Kate Brooks"), who filmed in Garamba for her documentary _The Last Animals_, thirteen park rangers and military personnel were killed defending Garamba between January 2015 and April 2017.[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Garamba_National_Park#cite_note-Brooks-22)

In 2017, National Geographic Documentary Films released _The Protectors: Walk in the Rangers' Shoes_, a short [virtual reality](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Virtual_reality "Virtual reality") documentary directed by [Kathryn Bigelow](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kathryn_Bigelow "Kathryn Bigelow") about the park's rangers and their efforts to protect Garamba's wildlife.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Garamba_National_Park#cite_note-NG-3)[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Garamba_National_Park#cite_note-Coyle-23) The [Tribeca Film Festival](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tribeca_Film_Festival "Tribeca Film Festival") posthumously awarded the Disruptor Award to rangers killed protecting Garamba "for their work and bravery in defending elephants", in April 2017.[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Garamba_National_Park#cite_note-Brooks-22)

### Mammals

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Garamba_National_Park&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Mammals")]

Garamba is home to 138 recorded mammal species,[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Garamba_National_Park#cite_note-Avant-6) including various [antelope](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antelope "Antelope"),[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Garamba_National_Park#cite_note-East-24)[African buffalo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/African_buffalo "African buffalo"), [African bush elephant](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/African_bush_elephant "African bush elephant"), [hyenas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hyena "Hyena"), [giant forest hog](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Giant_forest_hog "Giant forest hog"), [giraffes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Giraffe "Giraffe"), [hippopotamus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hippopotamus "Hippopotamus"), and lion.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Garamba_National_Park#cite_note-Canby-5)[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Garamba_National_Park#cite_note-Nicolon-12)[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Garamba_National_Park#cite_note-Dasgupta-17) The park hosts the country's only remaining population of giraffes, the Kordofan subspecies, and one of the country's largest remaining elephant populations.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Garamba_National_Park#cite_note-Canby-5)[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Garamba_National_Park#cite_note-Nicolon-12)

Garamba's elephants are considered a hybrid of the [African bush](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/African_bush_elephant "African bush elephant") and [African forest](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/African_forest_elephant "African forest elephant") subspecies.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Garamba_National_Park#cite_note-Canby-5) Poaching has reduced the park's elephant population in recent decades.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Garamba_National_Park#cite_note-Gettleman-4) There were around 2,800 elephants in 2011.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Garamba_National_Park#cite_note-Gettleman-4) In 2017, there were estimated to be fewer than 2,000 elephants in Garamba, a significant decline from the approximately 20,000 reported in the 1960s and 1970s.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Garamba_National_Park#cite_note-Canby-5)[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Garamba_National_Park#cite_note-NG-3)[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Garamba_National_Park#cite_note-Dasgupta-17) 22 elephants were killed in 2012,[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Garamba_National_Park#cite_note-Gettleman-4) and in 2014 poachers killed 68 of Garamba's elephants within two months.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Garamba_National_Park#cite_note-Dasgupta-17)[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Garamba_National_Park#cite_note-NYDN-25)[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Garamba_National_Park#cite_note-Min-26) Elephant poaching numbers declined from 98 in 2015 to three in 2022 in result to an effective law enforcement strategy.[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Garamba_National_Park#cite_note-27)

Reported giraffe population sizes have varied, but show a general decline in the 1990s and 2000s. The population's recorded peak was 300 in 1976, and more than 100 were reported in 2008.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Garamba_National_Park#cite_note-Nicolon-12) There were 356 giraffes in 1993, and only 86 by 2007.[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Garamba_National_Park#cite_note-TheTimes-28) There were 86 in 2003 and only 38 in 2016.[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Garamba_National_Park#cite_note-Hinckley-29) As of 2022, there were 71 giraffes in the park, and in 2024, over 80 Kordofan giraffes were allegedly present.[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Garamba_National_Park#cite_note-Parks-30) Poaching is the greatest threat to Garamba's giraffe population.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Garamba_National_Park#cite_note-Nicolon-12)[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Garamba_National_Park#cite_note-31)

The park once had the last wild population of the [northern white rhinoceros](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Northern_white_rhinoceros "Northern white rhinoceros").[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Garamba_National_Park#cite_note-Canby-5)[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Garamba_National_Park#cite_note-Gettleman-4)[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Garamba_National_Park#cite_note-Heale-10) Only fifteen northern white rhinos were reported in Garamba in the mid 1980s, prompting the park's inclusion on [UNESCO](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UNESCO "UNESCO")'s [List of World Heritage in Danger](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_World_Heritage_in_Danger "List of World Heritage in Danger").[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Garamba_National_Park#cite_note-Avant-6) In 2003–2004, there were reportedly between 20 and 25 white rhinos in the park.[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Garamba_National_Park#cite_note-Sieff-32)[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Garamba_National_Park#cite_note-Bisset-33)[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Garamba_National_Park#cite_note-Irish-34) In 2023, restoration efforts led to 16 white rhinos being moved from a private game reserve in South Africa to the park.[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Garamba_National_Park#cite_note-rhino-35)

### Birds

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Garamba_National_Park&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Birds")]

Some 286 bird species, including the [secretarybird](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Secretarybird "Secretarybird"),[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Garamba_National_Park#cite_note-Gettleman-4) have been recorded in the park.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Garamba_National_Park#cite_note-Avant-6) It has been designated an [Important Bird Area](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Important_Bird_Area "Important Bird Area") (IBA) by [BirdLife International](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BirdLife_International "BirdLife International") because it supports significant populations of many bird species.[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Garamba_National_Park#cite_note-bli-36)

### Threats

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Garamba_National_Park&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: Threats")]

Interactions between people and wild animals in and around the park has resulted in [human–wildlife conflict](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Human%E2%80%93wildlife_conflict "Human–wildlife conflict"). Local and South Sudanese poachers hunt for elephants, often in search of [ivory](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ivory_trade "Ivory trade").[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Garamba_National_Park#cite_note-Nicolon-12)[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Garamba_National_Park#cite_note-Dasgupta-17) Garamba's wildlife are also impacted by groups such as the Huda and [Wodaabe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wodaabe "Wodaabe") (or "Mbororo") seeking [pasture](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pasture "Pasture").[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Garamba_National_Park#cite_note-Nicolon-12)
